```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(here)

# custom functions
calc_mode <- function(x, na.rm = FALSE) {
  if (na.rm) x <- x[!is.na(x)]
  ux <- unique(x)
  ux[which.max(tabulate(match(x, ux)))]
}

```


## New Data: clean up and join 

### Step 1: Clean Up Dwell Data

The Hawaii data comes to us raw in text files, similar to Oahu. Here we will just generate the same summary tables as we did for Oahu. We will have to read in each excel file here and do some cleaning. 

This report should tell us:

- total number of TMKS assessed each year for Oahu
- how many TMKS are single owner versus multiple owner per year of data
- how many TMKS have more than one card (i.e. more than one building assessed on the parcel) per year
- Summary of bedrooms and bathrooms per year?


This might get long - the Hawaii dwell data is quite messy. A few notes from the data sent by the county: 

2010 - 2012 data did not come with extract formula sheets with them

I realized that specification docs were included for all years after 2012. I looked at them all side by side and there appear to be two distinct versions. The first (A) applies only to 2013, and 2019 - 2023. The second one (B) applies to 2014 - 2018.

They are actually identical until the year built column, which makes sense because when I was applying the ones above to different groups of years, the column that clued me into if it was working or not was year built. 

In A, yrbuilt is 434 to 437
In B, yrblt is 425 to 429

#### Step 1 Best Way
For Hawaii, Iʻm going to try a slightly different approach where I filter before worrying about the column parsing. Just to make things lighter 


```{r}

library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)
library(janitor)

# read in HI iws permits

iws_permit_data <- read_csv(file.path(data_dir, "osds/shared-data/2009_Present_IWSList_Permits.csv"))


# filter out just the permits in Hawaii, and create permit ID tracker

iws_hi_permits <- iws_permit_data %>% 
  mutate(tmk_char = as.character(TMK)) %>% 
  filter(str_starts(tmk_char,"3")) %>% 
  rename(full_taxid = tmk_char) %>%  
  rowid_to_column("permit_id") # 7347

tmks_permits <- iws_hi_permits$full_taxid

# function to go get and read in each text file, parse, and filter
read_and_filter_hi_dwell <- function(year, driver_dir, col_specs, tmks_permits) {
  file_path <- file.path(driver_dir,
                         "4_OSDS_N_Runoff/large-input-data/Dwelling_Data_Raw/Hawaii_DwellRaw_12182025",
                         as.character(year),
                         "DWELDAT.TXT")
  
  read_fwf(file_path,
           col_positions = col_specs,
           na = c("", "NA"),
           col_types = cols(.default = col_character())) %>%
    mutate(across(everything(), ~trimws(.))) %>%
    # Rename first two columns
    rename(jursi_id = 1, tmk = 2) %>%
    # Create tmk_13 and tmk_9
    mutate(
      tmk_13 = paste0(jursi_id, tmk),
      tmk_9  = substr(tmk_13, 1, nchar(tmk_13) - 4)
    ) %>%
    # Filter by the TMKs we care about
    filter(tmk_9 %in% tmks_permits)
}

# next, apply function for years that correspond to each Spec 

yearsA <- c(2019:2023)

yearsA_list <- map(yearsA, ~read_and_filter_hi_dwell(.x, driver_dir, colspec_A, tmks_permits))
yearsA_df <- do.call(rbind, yearsA_list)


yearsB <- c(2013:2018)

yearsB_list <- map(yearsB, ~read_and_filter_hi_dwell(.x, driver_dir, colspec_B, tmks_permits))
yearsB_df <- do.call(rbind, yearsB_list)


# experiment: try b on A years? this seems to work better

yearsAbyB_list <- map(yearsA, ~read_and_filter_hi_dwell(.x, driver_dir, colspec_B, tmks_permits))
yearsAbyB_df <- do.call(rbind, yearsAbyB_list) 

# last bit: try both col spec versions on 2010 - 2012. 
yearsC <- (2010:2012)
yearsCbyA_list <- map(yearsC, ~read_and_filter_hi_dwell(.x, driver_dir, colspec_A, tmks_permits))
yearsCbyA_df <- do.call(rbind, yearsCbyA_list)

yearsCbyB_list <- map(yearsC, ~read_and_filter_hi_dwell(.x, driver_dir, colspec_B, tmks_permits))
yearsCbyB_df <- do.call(rbind, yearsCbyB_list)

# weirdly, while A was close in column it was split, while B was not split just behind. But I think A i feel safer about

dwell_2010_2012 <- yearsCbyA_df %>% 
  mutate(year_built_fixed = paste0(YRBLT,substr(EFFYR,1,1))) %>% #paste together year and the first character of eff year
  mutate(effective_year_fixed = paste0(substr(EFFYR,2,nchar(EFFYR)), substr(COND,1,1))) %>% 
  clean_names() %>% 
  select(jursi_id,
         tmk,
         tmk_9,
         taxyr,
         card,
         fixbath,
         fixhalf,
         rmtot,
         rmbed,
         yrblt = year_built_fixed,
         effyr = effective_year_fixed)
  


# select colums needed and bind all together

dwell_2013_2023 <- rbind(yearsAbyB_df, yearsB_df) %>% 
  clean_names() %>% 
  select(jursi_id,
         tmk,
         tmk_9,
         taxyr,
         card,
         fixbath,
         fixhalf,
         rmtot,
         rmbed,
         yrblt,
         effyr)

# bind all together!


allyears_hi_dwell <- rbind(dwell_2010_2012, dwell_2013_2023) %>% 
  rename(full_taxid = tmk_9)



# save

write_csv(allyears_hi_dwell, 
          file.path(driver_dir,"4_OSDS_N_Runoff/output-data/dwellings/hi_dwell_clean_2010_2023_permitTMKonly.csv"))


```

Ok so it looks like col Spec B has worked really well for all years. Who knew! Iʻm going to quickly check for any mistakes below, then we can move on.

```{r}

# if starting here, read in HI clean dwelling data

allyears_hi_dwell <- read_csv(file.path(driver_dir,"4_OSDS_N_Runoff/output-data/dwellings/hi_dwell_clean_2010_2023_permitTMKonly.csv"))

# create new column with length of yearbuilt, and print unique instances

allyears_dwell$yearblt_length <- nchar(allyears_dwell$YRBLT)

unique(allyears_dwell$yearblt_length) # 4 and NA

# look at the NAS

allyears_dwell_yrblt_Na <- allyears_dwell %>% filter(is.na(yearblt_length))

# which years does this apply to?

unique(allyears_dwell_yrblt_Na$TAXYR) # since 2019

```

Hmm ok so I think I actually did not solve the parsing problem, and 2019 - 2023 did not parse correctly. Above, I went back and used col spec A on 2019 - 2023, and B for the rest. 

Lastly, we need to check if any of the dwellings with OSDS have updates since 2010 in their bedroom data. We'll re-run the same process above, but with a new list of tmks from the old osds dataset.I do this in Step 3b. 

### Step 2: Bring in IWS data

Here we join dwell data to the permit information for the ones that correspond to dwellings, and save the list of non-dwell TMKS.

```{r}

# read in clean dwelling data

allyears_hi_dwell <- read_csv(file.path(driver_dir,"4_OSDS_N_Runoff/output-data/dwellings/hi_dwell_clean_2010_2023_permitTMKonly.csv")) %>% 
  mutate(full_taxid = as.character(full_taxid))

# read in HI iws permits

iws_permit_data <- read_csv(file.path(data_dir, "osds/shared-data/2009_Present_IWSList_Permits.csv"))


# filter out just the permits in Hawaii, and create permit ID tracker

iws_hi_permits <- iws_permit_data %>% 
  mutate(tmk_char = as.character(TMK)) %>% 
  filter(str_starts(tmk_char,"3")) %>% 
  rename(full_taxid = tmk_char) %>%  
  rowid_to_column("permit_id") # 7347

tmks_permits <- iws_hi_permits$full_taxid

# execute join to see which tmks have dwell data

iws_hi_dwell_join <- inner_join(iws_hi_permits, allyears_hi_dwell, by = "full_taxid") %>% 
  distinct() # 69630 rows, 6011 TMKS
# also filter, this should have fewer rows but the same number of tmks

iws_hi_dwell_join_norepeats <- iws_hi_permits %>% 
  filter(full_taxid %in% allyears_hi_dwell$full_taxid) #6242 rows, 6011 tmks YAY

# now identify permits that donʻt have dwell data, and save 

iws_hi_NOdwell <- iws_hi_permits %>% 
  filter(full_taxid %!in% iws_hi_dwell_join$full_taxid) # 1105

write_csv(iws_hi_NOdwell,
         file.path(driver_dir,"4_OSDS_N_Runoff/output-data/qaqc/hi_iwspermits_nodwellinginfo.csv"))

```

**Results so Far**:
- There were 7347 permits issued for HI island over the past 10 years
- 6242 have dwelling information, and this represents 6011 tmks
- 1105 do not have dwelling information

### Step 2b: Clean and Pivot Permit Data

Instead of doing a bunch of stuff that identifies easy, tricky and hard scenarios, I'm condensing everything here into one big clean. 
are as follows: 
1. Assign class, using a custom function
2. Create master list (table 1)
3. Create tables 2 and 3 based on master list. 

```{r}

library(janitor)

# create a mater clean


## osds class assignment function 
# Define disposal types 
primary_disposal <- c("Bed", "Trench", "Infiltrators / Chambers", "ET Bed-Irrigation System", "Presby")
minimal_disposal <- c("Seepage Pit", "Cesspool-New")
unknown_disposal <- c("Other", "Unknown")

# Class assignment function 
assign_osds_class <- function(p_type, d_type) {
  case_when(
    p_type == "Septic Tank" & d_type %in% primary_disposal ~ "1",
    p_type == "Septic Tank" & d_type %in% c(minimal_disposal, unknown_disposal) ~ "2",
    p_type == "Septic Tank" & d_type == "Combination of two types" ~ "1",
    
    p_type %in% c("Compost Toilet", "Gray Water System", "Compost Toilet/Gray Water System") & 
      d_type %in% unknown_disposal ~ "3",
    p_type %in% c("Compost Toilet", "Compost Toilet/Gray Water System") & d_type == "Bed" ~ "1",
    p_type == "Gray Water System" & d_type %in% c("Bed", "Trench") ~ "3",
    
    p_type == "Aerobic Unit" & d_type %in% primary_disposal ~ "1",
    p_type == "Aerobic Unit" & d_type %in% minimal_disposal ~ "4",
    p_type == "Aerobic Unit" & d_type %in% unknown_disposal ~ "3",
    p_type == "Aerobic Unit" & d_type == "Combination of two types" ~ "1",
    
    p_type %in% c("Cesspool-New", "Cesspool-Existing") ~ "4",
    p_type %in% c("Presby (passive, NSF 40)", "Holding Tank (Government Only)", "Incinerating Toilet") ~ "1",
    
    p_type == "Other" & d_type %in% primary_disposal ~ "1",
    TRUE ~ "1" # Catch-all default based on your manual fix
  )
}


## clean up permits by adding a year column, assigning osds class, and trying to standardize the address

master_clean <- iws_hi_permits %>%
  clean_names() %>%
  mutate(
    approval_date = mdy(final_approval_date),
    year = year(approval_date),
    address_full = if_else(is.na(project_street_address2), 
                           project_street_address, 
                           paste(project_street_address, "-", project_street_address2)),
    address_lower = str_trim(str_to_lower(address_full)),
    osds_class = assign_osds_class(permit_type, disposal_type),
    dwelling_yn = ifelse(tmk %in% iws_hi_NOdwell$TMK,"no","yes")
  ) %>%
  select(-permit_id) %>% 
  distinct() # this removes any EXACT duplicates.

length(unique(master_clean$tmk))

# N rows = 7124 after distinct, 7347 before
# N tmks = 6818

# now create the three tables - bedroom will not be relevant for the non commercial #


### TABLE 1 #########

table1_tmk_registry <- master_clean %>%
  group_by(full_taxid) %>%
  summarize(
    n_permits = n(),
    n_years = n_distinct(year),
    n_addresses = n_distinct(address_lower),
    min_year = min(year),
    max_year = max(year),
    is_dwelling = any(full_taxid %in% allyears_hi_dwell$full_taxid),
    scenario = case_when(
      n_addresses == 1 & n_permits == 1 ~ "Simple",
      n_addresses > 1 ~ "Multi-Building",
      n_years > 1 ~ "Potential Upgrade",
      TRUE ~ "Multiple Permits Same Year"
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )


#### TABLE 2 A and 2 B ########

table2a_bedrooms <- allyears_hi_dwell %>%
  filter(full_taxid %in% master_clean$full_taxid) %>%
  mutate(rmbed = as.numeric(rmbed)) %>%
  group_by(full_taxid, taxyr) %>%
  summarize(
    total_beds = sum(rmbed, na.rm = TRUE),
    # mode_beds = calc_mode(rmbed, na.rm = TRUE), # Uncomment if you want mode instead
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = taxyr, values_from = total_beds, names_sort = TRUE) %>% 
  rename(tmk = full_taxid) %>% 
  rename_with(~ paste0("beds_", .), matches("^[0-9]"))


table2b_bedrooms <- allyears_hi_dwell %>%
  filter(full_taxid %in% master_clean$full_taxid) %>%
  mutate(rmbed = as.numeric(rmbed)) %>%
  group_by(full_taxid, taxyr) %>%
  summarize(
    #total_beds = sum(rmbed, na.rm = TRUE),
    mode_beds = calc_mode(rmbed, na.rm = TRUE), # Uncomment if you want mode instead
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = taxyr, values_from = mode_beds, names_sort = TRUE) %>% 
  rename(tmk = full_taxid)

#### TABLE 3 ####

table3_classes <- master_clean %>%
  group_by(full_taxid, year) %>%
  summarize(
    all_classes_text = paste(sort(unique(osds_class)), collapse = ", "),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(encoded_sum = 
    (str_detect(all_classes_text, "1") * 1) +
    (str_detect(all_classes_text, "2") * 2) +
    (str_detect(all_classes_text, "3") * 4) +
    (str_detect(all_classes_text, "4") * 8)
  ) %>%
  select(full_taxid, year, encoded_sum) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = year, values_from = encoded_sum, names_sort = TRUE) %>% 
  rename_with(~ paste0("osds_cl_", .), matches("^[0-9]")) %>% 
  rename(tmk = full_taxid)

# Filter out Commercial, ie dwell = no

table1_tmk_registry_commercial <- table1_tmk_registry %>% 
  filter(is_dwelling == FALSE)

```

```{r}
### Save

write_csv(table1_tmk_registry,
          file.path(driver_dir,"4_OSDS_N_Runoff/output-data/int/hi_tables/table1_tmk_registry_all.csv"))

write_csv(table2a_bedrooms,
          file.path(driver_dir,"4_OSDS_N_Runoff/output-data/int/hi_tables/table2a_bedrooms_sum.csv"))

write_csv(table2b_bedrooms,
          file.path(driver_dir,"4_OSDS_N_Runoff/output-data/int/hi_tables/table2b_bedrooms_mode.csv"))

write_csv(table3_classes,
          file.path(driver_dir,"4_OSDS_N_Runoff/output-data/int/hi_tables/table3_class_allcsv"))


## Read back in

hi_table1 <- read_csv(file.path(driver_dir,"4_OSDS_N_Runoff/output-data/int/hi_tables/table1_tmk_registry_all.csv"))

table2a_bedrooms <- read_csv(file.path(driver_dir,"4_OSDS_N_Runoff/output-data/int/hi_tables/table2a_bedrooms_sum.csv")) %>% 
  rename(tmk = full_taxid)

table3_classes <- read_csv(file.path(driver_dir,"4_OSDS_N_Runoff/output-data/int/hi_tables/table3_class_allcsv")) %>% 
  rename(tmk = full_taxid)
```

Ok so this works beautifully in that the bedroom table does not include any commercial tmks. Those will have their own table, which will specify "place", which dictates effluent, which 




## Step 3: Compare to Past Datasets to Complete the Time Series

```{r}

hi_otp <- read_csv(file.path(driver_dir,"4_OSDS_N_Runoff/large-input-data/OSDS_HIGIS_2010/On-site_Sewage_Disposal_Systems_-_Hawaii_Island.csv"))

unique(hi_otp$class) # weirdly this has no 4

```

So the Hawaii database has a similar format to the others, but also has a column with "source", indicating that someone has already gone through the processes of bringing in additional information for TMKS not in the Dwelling Assessment. This means that we should use this for our "mismatches" in the new data. There are also notes for all the commercial properties which is great!

UNFORTUNATELY there is no information about how effluent was calculated for non dwells as far as I can tell, but maybe some snooping around later will fix that. And, is a good reason to apply a standardized approach that matches the other islands.

According to the page: Source =  State of Hawaii Department of Health, May, 2017.

We also have these! Which are helpful:

PITT Code Values:   0  Timeshare (Maui only)   100’s*  Improved Residential   200’s  Apartment   300’s  Commercial   400’s  Industrial   500’s  Agricultural and Rural   600’s   Conservation   700’s   Hotel and Resort   800’s**  Unimproved Residential   900’s  Homeowner    999   Multiple PITT Codes for a single TMK   1000’s  Commercialized Residential (Maui only)      *  Kauai:  100 = Improved and Unimproved Residential   **  Kauai:  800 = Homestead Properties 

Also: lots of -9999 in class? And no class 4 or 5. That makes no sense. 

Some of this data is messy and yuck but there is also a lot of helpful work that it looks like the department of health did in 2017 (or Joey did?) 

Another weird thing about this data is that they dropped the year column. 

We only have classes 1 - 4 in this data. From the metadata, this
represents:

-   CLASS_I: Class I OSDS are those systems where the effluent is
    subjected to soil treatment
-   CLASS_II: Class II OSDS are septic systems discharging to a seepage
    pit.\
-   CLASS_III: Class III OSDS are aerobic systems discharging to a
    seepage pit.
-   CLASS_IV: Class IV OSDS are cesspools.\
-   EFFLUENT: The total effluent flux in million gallons per day
    discharged within the TMK parcel.
    
    
The `osds_class` column also does not have any 4s, just 1-3, and -9999. I'll use the same additive coding here as I did with Maui Nui, Kauai (and eventually Oahu): 

### Wastewater Class Encoding Reference Table

| Detected Classes | Encoded Sum | Description |
| :--- | :---: | :--- |
| **Class 1** | 1 | Cleanest Septic Type |
| **Class 2** | 2 | Secondary Septic Type |
| **Class 1 + 2** | 3 | **Combination of Class 1 + Class 2** |
| **Class 3** | 4 | Aerobic System |
| **Class 1 + 3** | 5 | Class 1 Septic + Aerobic |
| **Class 2 + 3** | 6 | Class 2 Septic + Aerobic |
| **Class 1 + 2 + 3** | 7 | Classes 1, 2, and 3 |
| **Class 4** | 8 | Cesspool |
| **Class 1 + 4** | 9 | Class 1 + Class 4 |
| **Class 2 + 4** | 10 | Class 2 + Class 4 |
| **Class 1 + 2 + 4** | 11 | Classes 1, 2, and 4 |
| **Class 3 + 4** | 12 | Aerobic + Class 4 |
| **Class 1 + 3 + 4** | 13 | Classes 1, 3, and 4 |
| **Class 2 + 3 + 4** | 14 | Classes 2, 3, and 4 |
| **All (1, 2, 3, 4)** | 15 | Full suite of permits |



```{r}
library(janitor)

hi_otp_clean <- hi_otp %>% 
  clean_names() %>% 
  select(tmk, starts_with("class"), "osds_qty") # n = 13351 

# apply additive encoding to match what we did with the new data

hi_otp_class_enc <- hi_otp_clean %>% 
  select(-class) %>% 
  pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("class"), names_to = "class", values_to = "quantity") %>% 
  filter(quantity != 0) %>% 
  rename(ttl_osds_2010 = osds_qty) %>% 
  mutate(osds_class_otp = case_when(
    class == "class_iv" ~ 8, # cesspool 
    class == "class_iii" ~ 4,
    class == "class_ii" ~ 2,
    class == "class_i" ~ 1
  )) %>%
  pivot_wider(id_cols = c("tmk","ttl_osds_2010"), names_from = "class", values_from = c("osds_class_otp")) %>%
  mutate(encoded_sum = rowSums(across(starts_with("class")), na.rm = TRUE))
  

# read in table 1. 

IWS_table1_tmk_registry <- read.csv(file.path(driver_dir,"4_OSDS_N_Runoff/output-data/int/hi_tables/table1_tmk_registry_all.csv"))


# Step 1: Split into three groups: NEW, UPDATED and UNCHANGED

otp_with_updates <- hi_otp_class_enc %>% 
  mutate(tmk = as.integer(tmk)) %>% 
  filter(tmk %in% IWS_table1_tmk_registry$full_taxid) # 2050 # add flag


otp_unchanged <- hi_otp_class_enc %>% 
  mutate(tmk = as.integer(tmk)) %>% 
  filter(tmk %!in% IWS_table1_tmk_registry$full_taxid) # 51009


new_permits <- IWS_table1_tmk_registry %>% 
  filter(full_taxid %!in% hi_otp_class_enc) # 6816 # flag

# add flags to the tmk registry in table 1 for UPDATES and NEW. 

IWS_table1_tmk_registry_wflags <- IWS_table1_tmk_registry %>% 
  mutate(status_since_otp = case_when(
    full_taxid %!in% otp_with_updates$tmk ~ "new permit application",
    full_taxid %in% otp_with_updates$tmk ~ "exists in otp",
    TRUE ~ "Z"
  )) %>% 
  rename(tmk = full_taxid)

```

##### Unchanged OSDS since OTP

```{r unchanged clean}

# --------------- Unchanged Data: Data Reshape and Merge ------------------------------------- #

# Here I take the tmks present in OTP that have not changed and reshape it to match the table 1, table 2 and table 3 datasets above. Add a flag, and then join to the rest. Columsn we need:

# - tmk
# - n permits (this is captured in the encoding)
# - n years (all one)
# - n addresses - we dont have address but we do have pittcodes
# - min and max year = 2009
# - dwelling flag = get from old data
# - scenario
# - status since otp = unchanged 


# ---------------- FIRST: Retrieve bedroom # for years after OTP ------------------- #

# Even if the permit didn't change, the dwelling may have. This would increase the effluent and therefore influence of that osds


# function to go get and read in each text file, parse, and filter
read_and_filter_hi_dwell <- function(year, driver_dir, col_specs, tmks_permits) {
  file_path <- file.path(driver_dir,
                         "4_OSDS_N_Runoff/large-input-data/Dwelling_Data_Raw/Hawaii_DwellRaw_12182025",
                         as.character(year),
                         "DWELDAT.TXT")
  
  read_fwf(file_path,
           col_positions = col_specs,
           na = c("", "NA"),
           col_types = cols(.default = col_character())) %>%
    mutate(across(everything(), ~trimws(.))) %>%
    # Rename first two columns
    rename(jursi_id = 1, tmk = 2) %>%
    # Create tmk_13 and tmk_9
    mutate(
      tmk_13 = paste0(jursi_id, tmk),
      tmk_9  = substr(tmk_13, 1, nchar(tmk_13) - 4)
    ) %>%
    # Filter by the TMKs we care about
    filter(tmk_9 %in% tmks_permits)
}

# years
yearsA <- (2019:2023)
yearsB <- (2013:2018)
yearsC <- (2010:2012)

# colspecs A and B (above, make sure they are read in)


# list of tmks - change name to match dwell data

otp_unchanged_tmks <- otp_unchanged_allinfo %>% select(full_taxid = tmk) #51009 
otp_UPDATED_allinfo_tmks <- otp_UPDATED_allinfo %>%  select(full_taxid = tmk)

otp_tmks_fordwellquery <- c(otp_unchanged_tmks$full_taxid, otp_UPDATED_allinfo_tmks$full_taxid) #53514

# apply function to years by group

yearsAbyB_list <- map(yearsA, ~read_and_filter_hi_dwell(.x, driver_dir, colspec_B, otp_tmks_fordwellquery))
yearsAbyB_df <- do.call(rbind, yearsAbyB_list) 

yearsB_list <- map(yearsB, ~read_and_filter_hi_dwell(.x, driver_dir, colspec_B, otp_tmks_fordwellquery))
yearsB_df <- do.call(rbind, yearsB_list)

yearsCbyA_list <- map(yearsC, ~read_and_filter_hi_dwell(.x, driver_dir, colspec_A, otp_tmks_fordwellquery))
yearsCbyA_df <- do.call(rbind, yearsCbyA_list)


# clean up and bind

otp_dwell_2010_2012 <- yearsCbyA_df %>% 
  mutate(year_built_fixed = paste0(YRBLT,substr(EFFYR,1,1))) %>% #paste together year and the first character of eff year
  mutate(effective_year_fixed = paste0(substr(EFFYR,2,nchar(EFFYR)), substr(COND,1,1))) %>% 
  clean_names() %>% 
  select(jursi_id,
         tmk,
         tmk_9,
         taxyr,
         card,
         fixbath,
         fixhalf,
         rmtot,
         rmbed,
         yrblt = year_built_fixed,
         effyr = effective_year_fixed)
  


# select colums needed and bind all together

otp_dwell_2013_2023 <- rbind(yearsAbyB_df, yearsB_df) %>% 
  clean_names() %>% 
  select(jursi_id,
         tmk,
         tmk_9,
         taxyr,
         card,
         fixbath,
         fixhalf,
         rmtot,
         rmbed,
         yrblt,
         effyr)

# bind all together!
otp_allyears_hi_dwell <- rbind(otp_dwell_2010_2012, otp_dwell_2013_2023) %>% 
  rename(full_taxid = tmk_9)

# save to dropbox 


write_csv(otp_allyears_hi_dwell, 
          file.path(driver_dir,"4_OSDS_N_Runoff/output-data/dwellings/hi_dwell_clean_2010_2023_otpTMKSonly.csv"))



# ---------------------------- SECOND: Create the three tables --------------------------- # 


otp_unchanged_allinfo <- hi_otp %>%
  mutate(tmk = as.integer(tmk)) %>% 
  filter(tmk %in% otp_unchanged$tmk) %>% 
  select(tmk, commercial, pittcode, ttl_bdrms, no_struct) %>% 
  left_join(., otp_unchanged, by = "tmk") %>% 
  select(-starts_with("class")) %>% 
  mutate(year = 2010)


otp_unchanged_table1 <- otp_unchanged_allinfo %>% 
  mutate(n_permits = case_when(
    encoded_sum %in% c(1,2,4,8) ~ 1,
    encoded_sum %in% c(3,5,6,9,10,12) ~ 2,
    encoded_sum %in% c(7,11,13,14) ~ 3,
    encoded_sum == 15 ~ 4,
    TRUE ~ 99999
  )) %>% 
  mutate(n_years = 1,
         n_addresses = "unknown",
         min_year = 2010,
         max_year = 2010,
         is_dwelling = ifelse(commercial == "Apartment/condo" | is.na(commercial),
                              TRUE,FALSE)) %>%
  mutate(
      scenario = case_when(
      n_permits == 1 & n_years == 1 ~ "Simple",
      n_addresses == "unknown" ~ "Unknown",
      n_years > 1 ~ "Potential Upgrade",
      TRUE ~ "Multiple Permits Same Year"
    ),
    status_since_otp = "unchanged since otp") %>% 
  select(-commercial, -pittcode,-ttl_bdrms, -no_struct, -ttl_osds_2010,-year,-encoded_sum)

# this one WILL include commercial 
otp_unchanged_table2_2010 <- otp_unchanged_allinfo %>% 
  select(tmk,year, ttl_bdrms) %>% 
  pivot_wider(id_cols = tmk,names_from = year, values_from = ttl_bdrms) %>% 
  mutate(tmk = as.character(tmk)) %>% 
  rename(OTP_2010 = `2010`)

# this one WON'T include commercial
otp_unchanged_table2_allyrs <- otp_allyears_hi_dwell %>%
  filter(full_taxid %in% otp_unchanged_table1$tmk) %>%
  mutate(rmbed = as.numeric(rmbed)) %>%
  group_by(full_taxid, taxyr) %>%
  summarize(
    total_beds = sum(rmbed, na.rm = TRUE),
    # mode_beds = calc_mode(rmbed, na.rm = TRUE), # Uncomment if you want mode instead
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = taxyr, values_from = total_beds, names_sort = TRUE) %>% 
  rename(tmk = full_taxid)

# all dwellings together - what drops out goes to table 4

possible_commercial_tmks <- setdiff(otp_unchanged_table2_2010$tmk, otp_unchanged_table2_allyrs$tmk)


# class
  
otp_unchanged_table3 <- otp_unchanged_allinfo %>% 
  select(tmk,year, encoded_sum) %>% 
  pivot_wider(id_cols = tmk,names_from = year, values_from = encoded_sum) %>% 
  rename_with(~ paste0("osds_cl_", .), matches("^[0-9]"))
  
# filter out the dwells that that didnt match in table 2 all years, see if they all have place assigment
otp_unchanged_table4_draft <- otp_unchanged_allinfo %>% 
  select(tmk, year, pitt_code = pittcode, commercial, ttl_bdrms) %>% 
  filter(tmk %in% possible_commercial_tmks) %>% 
  mutate(comm_assignment = case_when(
    # Exact Matches (High Priority)
    pitt_code == 0    ~ "Timeshare (Maui only)",
    pitt_code == 999  ~ "Multiple PITT Codes",
    
    # kauai Specifics (Assumes you have a 'county' column)
    # county == "Kauai" & pitt_code == 100 ~ "Improved and Unimproved Residential",
    # county == "Kauai" & pitt_code == 800 ~ "Homestead Properties",

    # Range Matches (The "Hundreds")
    pitt_code >= 1000 ~ "Commercialized Residential (Maui only)",
    pitt_code >= 100 & pitt_code < 200 ~ "Improved Residential",
    pitt_code >= 200 & pitt_code < 300 ~ "Apartment",
    pitt_code >= 300 & pitt_code < 400 ~ "Commercial",
    pitt_code >= 400 & pitt_code < 500 ~ "Industrial",
    pitt_code >= 500 & pitt_code < 600 ~ "Agricultural and Rural",
    pitt_code >= 600 & pitt_code < 700 ~ "Conservation",
    pitt_code >= 700 & pitt_code < 800 ~ "Hotel and Resort",
    pitt_code >= 800 & pitt_code < 900 ~ "Unimproved Residential",
    pitt_code >= 900 & pitt_code < 999 ~ "Homeowner",
    
    # Catch-all for anything else
    TRUE ~ "Unknown"
  ))

table4_summary <- otp_unchanged_table4_draft %>% 
  group_by(comm_assignment) %>% 
  summarize(
    types = length(tmk)
  )

# ------------------ It looks like someone has really put in the work here to figure out what is a dwelling and what isn't. Therefore, we'll re-assign TMKS that have bedrooms back into table 2. Anything that has a commercial assignment and bedrooms = 0, goes into table 4 ----------- #

addons_fortable2 <- otp_unchanged_table4_draft %>% 
  filter(is.na(commercial) & ttl_bdrms != 0) %>% 
  select(tmk, pitt_assigment = comm_assignment)
  #pivot_wider(id_cols = tmk, names_from = year, values_from = ttl_bdrms)# 2811. The only issue with these is that we dont have year built or year this was added into the database. so we'll assume they are active, but that may be an over inflation. ADD FLAG to TABLE 1!  

# Make sure all of the add ons area already in table 2
table_2_check <- otp_unchanged_table2_2010 %>% 
  filter(tmk %in% addons_fortable2$tmk)

# Add confirmed commercial to table 4
otp_unchanged_table4_cl <- otp_unchanged_table4_draft %>% 
  filter(!is.na(commercial) & ttl_bdrms == 0) %>%
  pivot_wider(id_cols = tmk,names_from = year, values_from = commercial) %>% 
  mutate(tmk = as.character(tmk))

# Merge new and old bedroom data to complete table 2. Manually filter out confirmed commercial, and apply gap fill logic:
# if OTP data has nothing, and dwell have nothing, check google places
# if OTP data has something and dwell have nothing, gapfill with OTP data


otp_unchanged_table2_2010_complete <- otp_unchanged_table2_allyrs %>% 
  full_join(otp_unchanged_table2_2010, by = "tmk") %>% 
  filter(tmk %!in% otp_unchanged_table4_cl$tmk) %>% 
  rename_with(~ paste0("new_", .), matches("^[0-9]")) %>% 
  mutate(gapfill_flag = if_else(
    OTP_2010 != 0 & rowSums(pick(starts_with("new_")) != 0, na.rm = TRUE) == 0,
    "Gap-filled with OTP value", 
    "Original dwell data"
  )) %>% 
  mutate(across(starts_with("new_"), ~ {
    # 1. helpers to check the state of ALL new columns for that row
    # (use 'cur_data()' to look at the other columns in the same row)
    row_all_na <- rowSums(!is.na(pick(starts_with("new_")))) == 0
    row_all_zero_or_na <- rowSums(pick(starts_with("new_")) != 0, na.rm = TRUE) == 0
    
    case_when(
      # condition 1: legacy is 0 and all new are NA -> Do nothing (keep as is)
      OTP_2010 == 0 & row_all_na ~ .,
      
      # condition 2: legacy != 0 AND (all are 0 OR all are NA) -> Use legacy
      OTP_2010 != 0 & row_all_zero_or_na ~ OTP_2010,
      
      # condition 3: some are NA but others > 0 -> Do nothing (keep as is)
      # (This is handled by the default behavior of case_when)
      TRUE ~ .
    )
  }))

# pull tmks to add flags 
tmks_tocheck_googplaces <- otp_unchanged_table2_2010_complete %>%
  filter(OTP_2010 == 0 & rowSums(!is.na(pick(starts_with("new_")))) == 0) %>%
  pull(tmk)

legacy_used_tmks <- otp_unchanged_table2_2010_complete %>%
  filter(gapfill_flag == "Gap-filled with OTP value") %>% 
  pull(tmk)

otp_unchanged_table2_2010_complete_cl <- otp_unchanged_table2_2010_complete %>% 
  select(-OTP_2010, -gapfill_flag)

# Add flags to Registry!

otp_unchanged_table1_final <- otp_unchanged_table1 %>% 
  left_join(., addons_fortable2, by = "tmk") %>%

new_and_unchanged_table3 <- otp_unchanged_table3 %>%

# Save tables we will return to later to update. 

write_csv(new_and_unchanged_tmk_registry,
          file.path(driver_dir,"4_OSDS_N_Runoff/output-data/int/hi_tables/table1_tmk_registry_NEW_and_UNCHANGED.csv"))

write_csv(new_and_unchanged_table2,
          file.path(driver_dir,"4_OSDS_N_Runoff/output-data/int/hi_tables/table2_bedrooms_NEW_and_UNCHANGED.csv"))

write_csv(new_and_unchanged_table3,
          file.path(driver_dir,"4_OSDS_N_Runoff/output-data/int/hi_tables/table3_classes_NEW_and_UNCHANGED.csv"))

write_csv(otp_unchanged_table4_cl,
          file.path(driver_dir,"4_OSDS_N_Runoff/output-data/int/hi_tables/table4_commercial_UNCHANGED_only.csv"))
```

#### Updated OTP

This one is a bit more complex. These tmks are already accounted for in our Tables 1 - 3 above, because they are updates. But, we want to know what those updates were. We also want to resolve any conflicts between new and old data. 

Like above, the person who updated this in 2017 may have had additional information that we do not get from the dwell data. 


``` {r updated}


# --------------- Updated Data: Compare, Reshape Merge ------------------------------------- #

  select(-starts_with("class"), -pittcode, -no_struct) %>%

  rename_with(., ~paste0("otp_",.x), .cols= !tmk)


table_2_2010 <- table2a_bedrooms %>%

    mutate(tmk = as.integer(tmk))

# check: are all the "updated" tmks already in table 2?

# no, missing a 262 (commercial) 


table_3_2010 <- table3_classes %>% 
  #rename(tmk = full_taxid) %>%

table3_updated <- table3_classes %>% filter(tmk %in% otp_UPDATED_allinfo$tmk) # yes, all accounted for

# create a year match flag
otp_updated_withIWS <- left_join(otp_UPDATED_allinfo, IWS_table1_tmk_registry_wflags, by = "tmk") %>% 
  mutate(tmk = as.character(tmk)) %>% 
  mutate(year_match = ifelse(max_year > 2010, "new permit app","no new permit since 2010"))

# create some flags for different bedroom scenarios
otp_updated_withNEWbeds <- left_join(otp_UPDATED_allinfo, IWS_table1_tmk_registry_wflags, by = "tmk") %>% 
  #filter(is_dwelling == TRUE) %>% 
  left_join(table_2_2010, by = "tmk")


year_cols <- otp_updated_withNEWbeds %>% select(starts_with("new")) %>% names()

otp_updated_with_BEDflags <- otp_updated_withNEWbeds %>% mutate(
     # CREATE MATCH INDEX: 
    # This finds the index (1, 2, 3...) of the first column that matches OTP bedrooms
    # We use matrix comparison (df[cols] == df$otp) to keep it vectorized
    match_index = {
      match_matrix <- pick(all_of(year_cols)) == otp_ttl_bdrms
      # replace NAs with FALSE so max.col doesn't trip
      match_matrix[is.na(match_matrix)] <- FALSE 
      
      # If a row has at least one match, get the index. Otherwise, NA.
      if_else(rowSums(match_matrix) > 0, max.col(match_matrix, ties.method = "first"), NA_integer_)
    },
    
    # CREATE MATCH NAME: Convert that index (e.g., 1) into the column name (e.g., "new_2010")
    match_name = year_cols[match_index],
    # COLUMN 1: The Match Year Flag
    # Priority: If it matches, show which one. Otherwise, it's unmatched.
    # match_status = case_when(
    #   !is.na(match_index) ~ paste0("Matches with ", match_name),
    #   TRUE                ~ "Unmatched"
    #),

    # COLUMN 2: The Direction of Change
    # Only applies to matches. We compare the OTP legacy to the matched year's value.
    bed_trend = case_when(
      otp_ttl_bdrms < newbeds_2023  ~ "Expansion since OTP",
      otp_ttl_bdrms > newbeds_2023  ~ "Shrink - double check",
      otp_ttl_bdrms == newbeds_2023 ~ "Perfect Match",
      TRUE                          ~ NA_character_
    ),

    # COLUMN 3: Data Presence (The "All Zeros/NAs" check)
    # Checks if ALL columns starting with 'NEW' are either 0 or NA
    data_presence = if_else(
      if_all(starts_with("newbeds"), ~ .x == 0 | is.na(.x)),
      "Empty (All 0 or NA)",
      "Bedrooms Recorded"
    )
  )

# remove commercial 


updated_table4_draft <- otp_updated_with_BEDflags %>% 
  filter(!is.na(otp_commercial)) # rows = 190

# get yearbuilt for these tmks
year_built_for_all <- allyears_hi_dwell %>%

otp_updated_with_BEDflags_gapfilled <- otp_updated_with_BEDflags %>%

  left_join(., year_built_for_all, by = "tmk") %>%
  # 1. Create the flags
  mutate(
    gapfill_flag = if_else(data_presence == "Empty (All 0 or NA)" & otp_ttl_bdrms > 0, 
                           "Gapfilled with OTP value", "Used dwell data")
  ) %>%
  # 2. Apply the Gap-fill
  mutate(across(starts_with("newbeds"), ~ {
    fill_condition <- data_presence == "Empty (All 0 or NA)" & otp_ttl_bdrms > 0
    if_else(fill_condition, as.numeric(otp_ttl_bdrms), as.numeric(.x))
  })) %>%
  # 3. Apply the CONSERVATIVE Year Built Correction
  mutate(across(starts_with("newbeds"), ~ {
    col_year <- as.numeric(str_extract(cur_column(), "\\d{4}"))
    
    case_when(
      # CONDITION A: If we DID NOT gap-fill this row, leave it exactly as is
      gapfill_flag == "Used dwell data" ~ as.numeric(.x),
      
      # CONDITION B: If we DID gap-fill, but house was built prior to 2010 or unknown, keep it
      is.na(year_built_combined) | year_built_combined <= 2010 ~ as.numeric(.x),
      
      # CONDITION C: If we DID gap-fill AND the house didn't exist yet, set to NA
      year_built_combined > col_year ~ NA_real_,
      
      # Fallback: Keep current value
      TRUE ~ as.numeric(.x)
    )
  }))

# METHODS NOTE: pre2009 column will retain otp value if there is no data for 2009 or 2010. if it matches what we have in 2009 or 2010, then we will just use those values and put NA in pre2009. 

update_logic_refined <- update_logic_df %>% 
  mutate(newpre_2009 = case_when(
    scenario_match_flag == "matched 2009 or 2010" ~ NA_real_,
    scenario_match_flag == "unmatched" | scenario_match_flag == "no data to compare" ~ as.numeric(legacy_val),
    TRUE ~ NA_real_
  )) %>% 
  select(tmk, newpre_2009, new2009, new2010, starts_with("new_201"), everything()) %>% 
  select(-class_history) %>% 
  unite("class_history", starts_with("new"), sep = "|", remove = FALSE) %>% 
  mutate(unique_story = sapply(str_split(class_history, "\\|"), function(x){
    x_clean <- x[!is.na(x) & x != "" & x != "NA"] # remove NAs and empty
    paste(unique(x_clean), collapse = "|")
  }),
  # 2. Define the Upgrade Scenarios
    upgrade_scenario = case_when(
      # Scenario 0: if empty or has no pipe, just a single state (no change)
      unique_story == "" | !str_detect(unique_story, "\\|") ~ "no upgrade detected",
     
       # Scenario 1: Single Cesspool (8) -> Any Septic/Aerobic (1, 2, or 4)
      # Regex: Look for 8, followed by anything, ending in 1, 2, or 4
      str_detect(unique_story, "^8\\|.*[1234]$") ~ "single cesspool upgraded to septic or aerobic",
      
      # Scenario 2: REPAIR Starts with 3, ends with 1 or 2
      str_detect(unique_story, "^3\\|.*[12]$") ~ "multiple septic with new permit: possible repair",
      
      # # SCENARIO 3: A "Cleaner" Septic Move (e.g., 2 or 4 upgraded to the "Cleanest" 1)
      str_detect(unique_story, "^[24]\\|>*1$") ~ "septic or aerobic system refined to cleanest type (Class 1)",
      
      # Scenario 3: Multiple OSDS (9-15) -> 1, 2, or 4
      # Regex: Look for any double-digit number between 9-15 followed by a better class
      str_detect(unique_story, "^(9|1[0-5])\\|.*[1234]$") ~ "multiple osds with cesspool upgraded",
      
      # Scenario 4: Multiple OSDS with cesspool (9 - 15) --> one cesspool 
      str_detect(unique_story, "^(9|1[0-5])\\|>*8$") ~ "multiple osds with new cesspool application",
      
      # DATA ERROR: Ends in 8 or 9 but started with something cleaner (1, 2, or 4)
      str_detect(unique_story, "^[1234567]\\|.*[8|9|1[0-5]]$") ~ "potential data error: backslide to cesspool",
      
      # LATERAL: Started Clean, Ended Clean, but not as Class 1 (e.g., 4|2 or 1|2)
      str_detect(unique_story, "^[123]\\|.*[123]$") ~ "lateral change (clean to clean)",
      
      # Catch-all
      TRUE ~ "other scenario"
    )) %>% 
  mutate(
    # upgrade_scenario = ifelse(legacy_val == 8 & unique_story == "1", "single cesspool upgraded to septic or aerobic", upgrade_scenario),
    upgrade_scenario = case_when(
      unique_story %in% "9|1|8" ~ "cesspool and septic - both repaired, no change",
      unique_story %in% "10|2|9" ~ "cesspool and septic 2 - septic repaired twice, cesspool once",
      TRUE ~ upgrade_scenario
      )
    )

update_logic_refined %>%
  filter(upgrade_scenario == "other scenario") %>%
  distinct(unique_story) %>%
  print()

# CLEANED UP VERSION

update_logic_refined_cl <- update_logic_df %>%

    scenario_match_flag == "matched 2009 or 2010" ~ NA_real_,
    scenario_match_flag %in% c("unmatched", "no data to compare") ~ legacy_val,
    TRUE ~ NA_real_
  )) %>% 
  select(tmk, newpre_2009, new2009, new2010, starts_with("new_201"), everything()) %>% 
  # Use rowwise to build the unique story without the split/paste overhead
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(unique_story = {
    vals <- c_across(starts_with("new"))
    vals <- vals[!is.na(vals) & vals != "" & vals != "NA"]
    paste(unique(vals), collapse = "|")
  }) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    upgrade_scenario = case_when(
      # High-priority special overrides
      unique_story == "9|1|8"  ~ "cesspool and septic - both repaired, no change",
      unique_story == "10|2|9" ~ "cesspool and septic 2 - septic repaired twice, cesspool once",
      unique_story == "7|9|1" ~ "potential data error: cesspool added, then possibly updated",

      str_detect(unique_story, "^3\\|.*[12]$") ~ "multiple septic with new permit: possible repair",
```

Important: Logic for resolving between otp dataset and IWS permits.
We want to preserve records of changes. There are a few types of mistmatches:
1) years match, but permits don't
2) years match, but bedrooms don't
3) years match, but we are missing bedroom information that the old data has?

Some text on the thinking so far: 

Where OTP matched to ANY year in bedrooms, I just left as is for now.

For dwellings that didnt match, i looked at the shrinkage amount: 
**Housing Data Methodology**
To construct a consistent 10-year longitudinal profile of residential capacity, we integrated historical bedroom counts (Column A) with contemporary annual tax assessment records (2000–2024). A primary challenge identified during data reconciliation was "negative bedroom growth," where tax-assessed bedroom counts were significantly lower (up to 4 rooms) than historical baselines. Given that tax assessments strictly adhere to legal building codes (e.g., egress and closet requirements), they often underrepresent informal or non-conforming living spaces. To maintain a realistic proxy for human habitation and land-use intensity, we implemented a "high-water mark" logic: historical values were used as a functional floor. This prevents artificial "capacity drops" in the timeline and ensures that unpermitted but occupied bedrooms—frequently found in local housing contexts—are captured in the longitudinal analysis.

We found that for HI Island, there are 87 permit entries that have a smaller number of bedrooms in the Tax assessment data than in the OTP dataset. ### Step 4: Apply bitmask logic to create "status" table from permit data

The additive encoding is what is known as a binary bit mask. Each class represents a power of 2, so every unique sum corresponds to exactly one combination of classes. 

We can think of table 3 as an "event" table, since it records the permit application event. However, we want to create a "status" table, which records the actual OSDS present on the property in each year, BASED on the events we know happened.

We can make multiple versions of this, using different math. In the first, I'll assume that:
1. If there was only one OSDS on the property, the new application is replacing it
2. If there were multiple OSDS on the property, the new application is replacing the grossest, ie highest class. This correspond to the largest power of 2 within the encoded value

This translates to the following math: 
1. Identify the largest power of 2 inside the current value.
2. Subtract that power of 2.
3. Add the new application value.

```{r}


library(tidyverse)

## ------------- 1. Helper functions ---------------- ##

# Function to find the largest power of 2 less than or equal to x
get_highest_class <- function(x) {
  if (x == 0) return(0)
  return(2^floor(log2(x)))
}

# Input data
# Example:  Year 1 value is 13 (8+4+1). Year 3 brings a "1".
applications <- c(13, 13, 1, 1, 1) 
active_status <- numeric(length(applications))

# Initialize
running_total <- applications[1]
active_status[1] <- running_total

# Logic loop 
for (i in 2:length(applications)) {
  # Trigger logic only if a NEW application value appears
  if (applications[i] != applications[i-1]) {
    
    # 1. Identify the highest bit currently active
    highest <- get_highest_class(running_total)
    
    # 2. Remove that highest bit
    # bitwAnd(x, bitwNot(y)) is the "proper" way to subtract a bit
    remaining <- bitwAnd(running_total, bitwNot(highest))
    
    # 3. Add the new application bitwise (OR)
    # This prevents 1 + 1 becoming 2
    running_total <- bitwOr(remaining, applications[i])
  }
  
  active_status[i] <- running_total
}


# wrapped in a nice function you can apply to a long-format table

# 1. Create a function for the logic
calculate_active_permits <- function(apps) {
  active_status <- numeric(length(apps))
  
  # Helper to find highest power of 2
  get_highest <- function(x) if (x == 0) 0 else 2^floor(log2(x))
  
  running_total <- apps[1]
  active_status[1] <- running_total
  
  for (i in 2:length(apps)) {
    # only trigger replacement if there is an application (>0)
    # If a new application value appears (it's an "event" year)
    #if (apps[i] != apps[i-1] & apps[i] != 0) 
    if(apps[i] >0){
      highest <- get_highest(running_total)
      # Remove highest bit, then Bitwise OR the new application
      running_total <- bitwOr(bitwAnd(running_total, bitwNot(highest)), apps[i])
    }
    active_status[i] <- running_total
  }
  return(active_status)
}

## ------------- 2. Read in data, reshape and apply ---------------- ##

table_3a <- read_csv(file.path(driver_dir,"4_OSDS_N_Runoff/output-data/int/hi_tables/table3_class_allcsv"))
  
table_3a_long <- table_3a %>% 
  pivot_longer(cols = -full_taxid, names_to = "Year", values_to = "Applied") %>% 
  mutate(Applied = replace_na(Applied,0))
  
table_3b_long <- table_3a_long %>% 
  arrange(full_taxid,Year) %>% 
  group_by(full_taxid) %>% 
  mutate(active_status = calculate_active_permits(Applied)) %>% 
  ungroup()
  
table_3b_wide <- table_3b_long %>% 
  pivot_wider(id_cols = full_taxid, names_from = Year,values_from = active_status)
```

```{r}
hi_otp_filtered_byNGI <- hi_otp %>% 
  filter(tmk %in% not_got_info$tmk) %>% 
  mutate(dwell_flag = "tmk not in dwelling data, but someone added bedroom #")# 132

# any others we did not account for? no

######### save the hi_otp by NGI so we can recombine with other dwelling data ################

write_csv(hi_otp_filtered_byNGI,
          file.path())

```

Ok! So, the Non-dwelling data is somewhat solved for Big Island. Here is the breakdown:
- 289 are known commercial locations
- 816 are not known commercial locations, but whoever updated this last has marked all of them with source = something other than Dwell Data. But the good news is that we now have all the info needed to calculate old effluent + if these were upgraded!

```{r}

# create the two tables for the commercial locations

########### table 1: tmk + key identifying info

table_1 <- got_info %>% 
  select(permit_id,tmk, island, starts_with("project"), final_approval_date, commercial_from_otp)

############# table 2: class by year. we need to assign class to the new data, and reshape the old data. 

# disposal types by treatment

minimal_treatment <- c("Seepage Pit",
                       "Cesspool-New")

primary_treatment <- c("Bed",
                       "Trench",
                       "Infiltrators / Chambers",
                       "ET Bed-Irrigation System",
                       "Presby")

unknown_treatment <- c("Other","Unknown")

combo_treatment <- c("Combination of two types")

hi_commercial_odsd_YearClasstable <- got_info %>% 
  select(permit_id, tmk, project_street_address, project_street_address2, final_approval_date, permit_type, disposal_type, ends_with("from_otp")) %>% 
  select(-class_from_otp) %>% 
  mutate(new_osds_class = case_when(
    permit_type == "Septic Tank" & disposal_type %in% primary_treatment ~"1",
    permit_type == "Septic Tank" & disposal_type %in% minimal_treatment ~"2",
    permit_type == "Septic Tank" & disposal_type %in% unknown_treatment ~ "2", 
    permit_type == "Septic Tank" & disposal_type %in% combo_treatment ~ "1", 
    permit_type %in% c("Compost Toilet","Gray Water System","Compost Toilet/Gray Water System") & disposal_type %in% c("Other","Unknown")  ~ "3",
    permit_type %in% c("Compost Toilet","Compost Toilet/Gray Water System") & disposal_type == "Bed" ~ "1",
    permit_type == "Gray Water System" & disposal_type %in% c("Bed","Trench") ~ "3",
    permit_type == "Aerobic Unit" & disposal_type %in% minimal_treatment ~ "4",
    permit_type == "Cesspool-New" ~ "4",
    permit_type == "Cesspool-Existing" ~ "4",
    permit_type == "Aerobic Unit" & disposal_type %in% primary_treatment ~ "1",
    permit_type == "Aerobic Unit" & disposal_type %in% unknown_treatment ~ "3",
    permit_type == "Aerobic Unit" & disposal_type %in% combo_treatment ~ "1",
    permit_type == "Presby (passive, NSF 40)" ~ "1",
    permit_type == "Holding Tank (Government Only)" ~ "1",
    permit_type == "Incinerating Toilet" ~ "1",
    permit_type == "Other" & disposal_type %in% primary_treatment ~ "1", #because it getting soil treatment?
    TRUE ~ "Can't assign MB" # the only one I couldnt assign just had some extra notes on the permit type
  )) %>% 
  mutate(approval_date = mdy(final_approval_date),
         year = year(approval_date))

hi_commercial_odsd_new_clean <- hi_commercial_odsd_YearClasstable %>% 
  select(permit_id, tmk,starts_with("project"),final_approval_date,year,new_osds_class) %>% 
  pivot_wider(id_cols = c("permit_id","tmk","project_street_address","project_street_address2","final_approval_date"), names_from = year, values_from = new_osds_class)

hi_commercial_osds_olds <- got_info %>% 
  select(permit_id,tmk,project_street_address, project_street_address2,final_approval_date, ends_with("from_otp")) %>% 
  pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("class"), names_to = "class", values_to = "quantity") %>% 
  filter(quantity != -9999) %>% 
  mutate(year = 2010) %>% 
  rename(ttl_osds_2010 = osds_qty_from_otp) %>% 
  mutate(osds_class_otp = case_when(
    str_detect(class, "class_iv") ~ 8, # cesspool 
    str_detect(class, "class_iii") ~ 4,
    str_detect(class, "class_ii") ~ 2,
    str_detect(class, "class_i") ~ 1
  )) %>%
  pivot_wider(id_cols = c("permit_id","tmk","project_street_address","final_approval_date","ttl_osds_2010"), names_from = c("class","year"), values_from = c("osds_class_otp")) %>%
  select(-class_from_otp_2010) %>% 
  mutate(combo_code = rowSums(across(starts_with("class")), na.rm = TRUE))

# join together

hi_commercial_olds_cl <- hi_commercial_osds_olds %>% 
  select(-starts_with("class")) %>% 
  rename(prior_class = combo_code)


table_2_final <- left_join(hi_commercial_olds_cl,hi_commercial_odsd_new_clean, by = c(
  "permit_id",
  "tmk",
  "project_street_address",
  "final_approval_date"
))

# use anti join to check that all of info in table 1 are in table 2

missing_rows <- anti_join(table_1, table_2_final, by = c(
  "permit_id",
  "tmk",
  "project_street_address",
  "final_approval_date"
)) # 0, yay!!



# save to drop box

write_csv(table1,
          file.path(driver_dir,"4_OSDS_N_Runoff/output-data/commercial_finaltables/hi_comm_table1.csv"))

write_csv(table_2_final,
          file.path(driver_dir,"4_OSDS_N_Runoff/output-data/commercial_finaltables/hi_comm_table2.csv"))

```
